news.title: Alonso on Martinez: 'He has this aura to influence'
news.body_en: Xabi Alonso was happy with the impact Emi Martinez made on his Chelsea debut and believes the goalkeeper’s ‘aura to influence’ will help the Blues throughout the season. The Argentine international's arrival from Aston Villa was confirmed this (Sunday) morning. Martinez signed a three-year contract at Stamford Bridge and went straight into our starting XI for Brighton and Hove Albion's visit. Martinez looked instantly at home and produced several impressive reaction stops throughout our 4-3 victory, which came through goals from Romeo Lavia, Pedro Neto, Joao Pedro and Cole Palmer. Alonso was not surprised by the ease with which Martinez settled into the Chelsea side, and only expects the goalkeeper's influence to increase going forward. He said: 'Emi is a World Cup winner, is 33 years old, and is very experienced. I spoke with him yesterday (Saturday) and we talked about the game and our team. He felt ready, and I don’t have to tell him many things for him to perform. 'Even today, while a goalkeeper wants to keep a clean sheet, I am happy with his impact. He has been in the building just 48 hours, so now we will have a whole week to prepare for the next one. ‘Day by day, we will feel this presence because he has this charisma, this aura to influence and have a very positive connection with the rest of the team.’

news.title: Match gallery: Blues score four to overcome Seagulls
Xabi Alonso on overcoming Brighton and Moises Caicedo injury
news.body_en: Chelsea manager Xabi Alonso emphasised the ‘value’ of this afternoon's 4-3 victory over Brighton and Hove Albion – and provided an update on Moises Caicedo after the midfielder was forced off with an injury in the second half. For 32 minutes of the contest at Stamford Bridge, the Blues were in full control. We opened the scoring early, with Romeo Lavia converting from close range for his first Chelsea goal, before Pedro Neto and Joao Pedro then found the net. Brighton reacted, though. They reduced the deficit before the interval through Malick Yalcouye and pulled another goal back when Joao Pedro turned a cross into the Blues’ net. However, Alonso’s players displayed their resilience to respond and re-establish our advantage, as Cole Palmer curled an excellent shot home from 20 yards. That proved enough to secure all three points, despite a late consolation from Pascal Gross. Alonso once again highlighted that there are improvements for his side to make in the weeks ahead, but he was pleased the Blues had overcome a difficult opponent to make it two wins from two Premier League fixtures at the start of the campaign. ‘All the wins I enjoy a lot, but it was a game that in different moments had different feelings,' Alonso explained in his post-match press conference. 'In the end, we’re happy with the result. We value this win against a very good opponent who have been tough in the last few years. We are happy with that, and there are things and moments that we have done well, but it’s a process to keep on learning and improving. Usually, that is easier with a win.’ The one negative of the afternoon was Caicedo's injury. The Ecuadorian midfielder missed our opening two fixtures of the season but was introduced from the substitutes' bench midway through the second period. However, 13 minutes after coming on, Caicedo was forced off and replaced by Valentin Barco, who helped the Blues get over the line. 'He was cautious to stop and say his feeling wasn’t the best,' Alonso replied when asked about the midfielder's injury after the game. 'We need to assess during the week, but it wasn’t something new.’

news.title: Highlights: Chelsea 4-3 Brighton
Alonso reflects on victory over Brighton
Lavia reacts to his first Chelsea goal!
Match report: Chelsea 4-3 Brighton
news.body_en: Romeo Lavia, Pedro Neto, Joao Pedro and Cole Palmer were all on target as the Blues made it three wins from three games with an entertaining 4-3 victory over Brighton and Hove Albion. We were once again free-flowing in attack and opened up a three-goal advantage after just 32 minutes. Lavia netted his first Chelsea goal to break the deadlock after four minutes, and both Neto and Joao Pedro found the net with clinical finishes from inside the penalty area. Brighton reduced the deficit before interval via Malick Yalcouye, and grabbed a second just after the hour-mark when Joao Pedro deflected a cross into our net. Yet Alonso's side, as they did against Fulham, showed the right response to pressure and, with 16 minutes to play, Palmer swept home a 20-yard strike. The Seagulls did grab a late third – Pascal Gross heading home – but it proved nothing more than a late consolation. Alonso made seven changes to the side that started our Carabao Cup second-round victory over Luton Town on Thursday Emi Martinez, whose signing was confirmed earlier in the day, started in goal. Wesley Fofana, Maxence Lacroix and Levi Colwill were the back three, with Neto and Jorrel Hato at wing-back. Lavia was partnered in midfield by Malo Gusto, and the front three was Palmer, Morgan Rogers and Joao Pedro. Before the action got underway, there were touching tributes to two influential Chelsea figures who passed away this summer: our second all-time highest goalscorer, Bobby Tambling, and our former chairman, Ken Bates. Both will be missed. At Fulham on Monday night, the Blues made a rapid start and were ahead inside 35 seconds. Our opener didn't arrive quite as early against the Seagulls, but just four minutes were on the clock. Neto was heavily involved, as the Portugal international won and delivered a corner that Joao Pedro met at the near post. Mats Wieffer got back onto the line to block, but a mix-up with goalkeeper Bart Verbruggen saw the ball fall to Lavia, who nudged a shot over the line for his first Chelsea goal. The Blues were firmly on top. We moved the ball confidently across the pitch and carried a threat whenever we advanced into Brighton's defensive third. And ten minutes after going ahead, we fashioned our second goal of the contest. Rogers was the creator, collecting a Joao Pedro knock-down and forcing his way past Mario Vuskovic. The England international squared the ball into the penalty area, and Neto burst forward to finish beyond Verbruggen. We should have had a third midway through the half, as Neto chased down and brushed aside Ferdi Kadıoglu and played a pass to Joao Pedro. The Brazilian took a touch, which sat down two Brighton defenders, but he guided his finish from 12 yards wide. Martinez, aside from coming to collect a couple of crosses, had little work to do in the opening half-hour. He did have to produce a smart reaction stop, though, when Yalcouye prodded a cross toward goal. Joao Pedro – booed throughout by the supporters of his former club – briefly silenced the away end with a deserved 32nd-minute goal. Hato was instrumental, exchanging passes in our half with Rogers and surging upfield with the ball. Wieffer was unable to keep up with the Dutchman, who fed the ball to Joao Pedro and the Blues' No.9 made no mistake with his finish. Unfortunately, our three-goal advantage was quickly reduced as Brighton pulled a goal back through Yalcouye, who rifled a volley in off the post after Martinez had denied Diego Gomez. Before the interval, each side created one further chance: Rogers came close for the Blues with a shot from distance that flashed past the post, while Gomez headed wide. The second period remained an open affair – perhaps too much for Alonso's liking. Brighton made better use of the space and caused the Blues problems. Many of the Seagulls' chances fell to Gomez. The Paraguayan forward dragged a shot wide before missing a close-range header from a free-kick. It was a chance he should have scored. Our threat remained and Neto did excellently once again to shrug off Kadıoglu and break into the box. His near-post effort was saved and, on the rebound, Rogers whipped a cross into the six-yard box for Palmer, who could only volley over. Martinez's first big save in a Chelsea shirt came soon after, as he reacted excellently to push wide a shot from Gomez. Unfortunately, from the resulting corner, the ball was worked to Pascal Gross, whose pass deflected off Joao Pedro and ended in our net. Alonso soon turned to his bench. Josh Acheampong, Reece James and Moises Caicedo, playing his first minutes of the season, were introduced. The booked Fofana, Lavia and Neto were replaced. Our changes didn't immediately quell the Brighton tide, and Martinez had to save well from a powerful drive from Olivier Boscagli. It was an important moment as, five minutes later, the Blues struck our fourth goal of the game. The goal had shades of our first, as Joao Pedro controlled and laid off a throw-in. This time, Palmer collected the ball, advanced 20 yards, and then curled a shot expertly beyond Verbruggen. Sixteen minutes remained – and the Blues worked hard to see out the contest. We shifted into a 5-4-1 shape, which largely kept Brighton outside our box, and enabled Joao Pedro to lead several counter-attacks, which were often stopped illegally by Brighton defenders. There were five minutes of stoppage time and it appeared there would be no more goals added to the scoreline. However, in the final action of the game, a long Brighton throw was flicked on and headed home by Gross. It proved too late to alter the destination of the points, with Alonso's side taking six from our opening two top-flight fixtures. We travel across London next weekend to face Arsenal at the Emirates Stadium on Sunday 6 September. Kick-off is scheduled for 4.30pm (UK time). Chelsea: Martinez; Fofana (Acheampong 68), Lacroix, Colwill (c) (Chavarria 72); Neto (Caicedo 68, Barco 82), Gusto, Lavia (James 68), Hato; Palmer, Rogers; Joao Pedro.Chelsea substitutes: Penders, Caicedo, Gittens, Estevao Willian, Welbeck.Goalscorers: Lavia 4, Neto 14, Joao Pedro 32Booked: Fofana 55 Brighton: Verbruggen, Wieffer (Costinha 80), Vuskovic, Dunk, Kadioglu; Gross, Boscagli; Gomez, Yalcouye (Osman 74), De Cuyper; Kostoulas Brighton substitutes: Steele, Struijk, Hadjam, Cozier-Duberry, O'Riley, OriolaGoalscorers: Yalcouye 35, Joao Pedro og 62, Gross 90+6Booked: Dunk 70, Boscagli 89, Costinha 90+1

news.title: Xabi Alonso on why Martinez starts
news.body_en: Xabi Alonso has spoken of his delight at recruiting Emi Martinez and revealed why he has decided to hand the Argentina international a debut today. The goalkeeper completed his switch from Aston Villa earlier today and starts between the sticks as we face Brighton at Stamford Bridge today. Alonso explained the reasoning behind that decision when speaking pre-match earlier today. ‘We are very happy with Emi and we are delighted to have him here at Chelsea,’ Alonso said of Martinez ahead of his Blues debut. ‘To have such a goalkeeper of this stature, of this personality, it’s very good for us. ‘I think that he will bring lots of qualities, and I'm sure that he can have a straight impact, and that's why we decided that he’s ready to play straightaway.’

news.title: Confirmed Chelsea line up vs Brighton
news.body_en: Emi Martinez makes his Chelsea debut as one of seven changes made to the Blues side by Xabi Alonso for this afternoon's Premier League clash against Brighton and Hove Albion. After starting our top-flight campaign with a victory at Fulham, and then defeating Luton Town in the Carabao Cup, the Blues are looking to make it three wins from three under Alonso, who was appointed manager earlier this summer. Martinez's signing from Aston Villa was confirmed this morning, and the Argentine goalkeeper goes straight into the starting XI to make his debut in front of the Stamford Bridge faithful. The 33-year-old will be protected by a back three consisting of Wesley Fofana, Maxence Lacroix and Levi Colwill – who skippers Chelsea today against his former loan club – with Pedro Neto and Jorrel Hato expected as the right and left wing-backs. Romeo Lavia looks set to be partnered by Malo Gusto in midfield, while Alonso has reverted to the attack that started against Fulham on Monday night. Each of Cole Palmer, Morgan Rogers and Joao Pedro scored in the game and will hope to do the same against the Seagulls. Danny Welbeck, who netted against Luton on Thursday night, starts on the bench against his former club, as do former Albion duo Moises Caicedo and Valentin Barco. Chelsea: Martinez; Fofana, Lacroix, Colwill (c); Neto, Gusto, Lavia, Hato; Palmer, Rogers; Joao Pedro. Emiliano Martinez signs for Chelsea!
news.body_en: Chelsea is delighted to announce the signing of Argentinian international Emiliano Martínez from Aston Villa. The 33-year-old goalkeeper, who won the World Cup in 2022, has signed a three-year deal with the Blues. 'I’m delighted to be at this football club,' Martinez said. 'Coming to Chelsea, for me and my family, was an easy decision to make and I’m just over the moon - I can’t wait to get started. 'I want to be successful here. I'm someone who wants to win at everything I do and I want to bring that here to this football club because it’s a football club that wins titles, so I think it’s a good match. 'I’m all passion and I play with my heart. I will give 100 per cent every game, every training session to make the club, my teammates and the supporters proud.' Having started his career in the youth system of Independiente, Martinez completed a move to Arsenal in August 2010, aged 17. After several loans to gain first-team experience, he became a regular for Arsenal in the 2019/20 campaign, starting the last 11 matches and winning the FA Cup. He won the Community Shield at the start of the following season before signing for Aston Villa in September 2020. During his time in the Midlands, Martinez established himself as one of the world’s leading goalkeepers. He made 256 appearances for Villa across six seasons and lifted the UEFA Europa League in May. Martinez made his international debut in June 2021 and has since been Argentina’s first-choice goalkeeper, earning 67 caps for his country. He has twice won the Copa America (2021 and 2024) with La Albiceleste and lifted the World Cup in 2022. Following those successes, Martinez received the Yashin Trophy, awarded to the world’s best-performing goalkeeper, at the 2023 and 2024 Ballon d’Or ceremonies.

news.title: Watch Emi Martinez's first interview as a Chelsea player
news.body_en: England has been home to Emi Martinez for almost 17 years. Yet while the country has shaped him as a person and a player, it is the values instilled while growing up in the Argentine city of Mar del Plata that have underpinned his career. Martinez officially began his journey in the English game – and eventually to becoming a Chelsea player – in August 2010. He had developed a reputation as one of South America's most promising goalkeepers while in the Independiente youth system and earned a move to Arsenal. Far away from home, Martinez had to adapt quickly. Within a year, he had learned English and passed his driving test. Yet on the pitch, it took far longer for the goalkeeper to make his mark. There were several loans in the Football League, and a brief spell in La Liga with Getafe, but as the 2019/20 campaign reached its conclusion, Martinez got a run in the Arsenal first team and never looked back. He lifted the FA Cup and the Community Shield before joining Aston Villa. During Martinez's time in the Midlands, he established himself as Argentina's first-choice goalkeeper and lifted two Copa Americas and a FIFA World Cup. In each of those triumphs, Martinez's drive and determination have shone through. And that mentality was formed in his childhood, as he explained in his first interview since becoming a Blue, which you can watch in full for free above. 'Becoming a footballer was always to help my family, to get them a better life and take them out of poverty,' Martinez explained. 'That drive is still in my football career. It doesn’t matter what I’ve won or where I’ve reached, I want more. 'I want them to be proud of me. Now I’ve got kids, I want them to see nothing comes easy in life. So I am still competing and I want more.’ Martinez has joined the Blues after six seasons at Villa Park, during which he twice received the Yashin Trophy, awarded to the world's best-performing goalkeeper. Now 33 years old, Martinez has no intention of settling on his former glories. He knows the expectations that come with being a Chelsea player and wants to match them throughout his time at Stamford Bridge. ‘I give 100 per cent every game and, when you see me play every day or in training sessions, I give you my all,' he says. 'I try to win every game; it doesn’t matter who we play against. I am bringing that here to this club because it’s a winning club that wins titles and wins things.'

news.title: Alonso: Now is the time to deliver
news.body_en: Xabi Alonso wants to repay the Chelsea supporters for their warm welcome with victory in an early test of our Premier League credentials on home soil against Brighton & Hove Albion. Our new manager has already experienced the support of the home crowd at Stamford Bridge on two occasions, when we beat Real Sociedad in our final friendly of pre-season and then defeated Luton Town to book our place in the Carabao Cup third round on Thursday evening. For the first home Premier League fixture of Alonso’s reign, Brighton are the visitors to west London in a 2pm kick-off on Sunday afternoon, with the Spaniard expecting another good reception for him and his team from the Blues fans. ‘It’s nice,’ responded Alonso. ‘We are happy to have that support and myself to have this welcome from the fans. ‘I have felt since the first day I was here that they were happy that we were starting this time together. Now is the time to deliver and the time to show it every weekend. ‘We’ve had two games and it’s a good start, but it’s still early days. On Sunday, we have a good game, a good test, to see where we are. ‘We will have bumps in the road, for sure, and we need to prepare for that. How we react, how we stick together, how we keep the mentality will be important. ‘So it’s early days and there have been good things, but there are things to develop and progress as well.’ Alonso has faced Brighton’s manager before, during his time at Bayer Leverkusen, leaving the Spaniard expecting a tough but important test of Chelsea’s early season progress from Fabian Hurzeler’s Seagulls side. ‘I know him very well from Germany, from St Pauli,’ added Alonso. ‘He is developing the team with new players. ‘They are a very intense team that do interesting things. So that’s why it’s going to be a good clash and a good test on Sunday.’

news.title: Let's make this our season 🙌
Chelsea vs Brighton: All you need to know
news.body_en: Bank Holiday weekend used to mean Londoners piling onto trains bound for the seaside, but this weekend Brighton & Hove Albion come to Chelsea. Club historian Rick Glanvill and club statistician Paul Dutton look ahead to a 2pm kick-off at Stamford Bridge with Premier League points on the line. Like Fulham away on Monday, this was a fixture the world champions lost last time around after having a player sent off. The 10 men in royal blue led 1-0 but were eventually downed 3-1 with Danny Welbeck, now under Xabi Alonso’s direction, among the visitors’ stoppage-time scorers. In fact the Blues have not beaten the Seagulls since Cole Palmer’s 10-minute hat-trick inspired a 4-2 victory at the Bridge in September 2024. On Thursday the visitors completed the job against Tromso to qualify for the UEFA Conference League proper, only their second European campaign. Last time they had to fulfil European midweeks, in 2023/24, they slipped from the previous sixth-place Premier League finish to 11th. Also on Thursday, Chelsea’s first home game of the season ended in a 2-0 victory over Luton Town, with Welbeck opening his Blues account. The Londoners can now secure three consecutive wins on all fronts for the first time since January (a run of five). Xabi Alonso is hopeful Chelsea midfielder Moises Caicedo will be ready to face Brighton on Sunday, and confirmed Levi Colwill and Geovany Quenda are in contention to face the Seagulls after missing the win over Luton. 'There were no issues [with Colwill and Quenda], and the plan is that they are training and preparing for the game on Sunday,' said Alonso in his pre-match press conference on Thursday night. 'He [Caicedo] is hopefully training and we are hopeful that he can be involved, but we need to check. No decision has been made.’ One player expected to be in contention to return for the Blues on Sunday is Wesley Fofana, who served the second of his two-match suspension against Luton. Summer signing Jordan Henderson may need more time, with Alonso stating that the Blues are waiting for him to be given the 'green light to play soon' following the injury he sustained during the World Cup. Chelsea have won just one of our past seven first home league games of the campaign, a 3-0 victory over Crystal Palace in 2021 with goals from Marcos Alonso, Christian Pulisic and debutant Trevoh Chalobah's first for the club. The remainder of that run comprises four draws and three losses, but it was not always such hard going at the Bridge. The Blues have won 20 of our previous 34 opening home games in the Premier League era, drawing 10 and losing four. The first of those victories came against Norwich City in 1994, as Glenn Hoddle’s project entered its second season. With the Shed End removed for redevelopment, goals from Frank Sinclair and Paul Furlong either side of the break settled the score. In 1999, a stellar set of goal scorers saw off a decent Sunderland side 4-0 – Gus Poyet (two), Gianfranco Zola and Tore Andre Flo – and a year later Mario Stanic made his mark with a stunning volley during a 4-2 romp against West Ham United. Then, in 2004, the game was forgettable but the result was vital, as Jose Mourinho’s management began with a 1-0 win against title rivals Manchester United thanks to Eidur Gudjohnsen. Three years later, United’s ’noisy neighbours’ Man City were taken apart by goals from iconic trio John Terry, Frank Lampard and Didier Drogba, while in 2010, 1997 FA Cup hero Roberto Di Matteo was shown no mercy as the Blues hit his West Bromwich Albion team for six – a club record for a curtain-raiser at the Bridge. A fine record of opening-day success heralding a title win was upheld in 2016, as Antonio Conte savoured a 2-1 derby defeat of West Ham, ahead of what proved another glorious campaign. Chelsea (1.96) and Brighton (3.54) recorded the highest expected goals tallies over the opening weekend of the Premier League. The Seagulls have scored three goals in each of their past three Premier League encounters with the Blues. Welbeck scored three of those. Following our 3-2 victory at Fulham, Chelsea have won six of the past seven opening away fixtures of the Premier League season. Thanks to Monday’s west London derby win, the world champions are already three points up on last season’s corresponding Premier League fixtures. Victory over Brighton would make that six. Chelsea’s run of 17 league outings without a clean sheet is the longest for the club since the same number in 1991, which ended with the Blues winning 1-0 at Sheffield United on 3 September – straight after a 4-1 home win against Luton Town. Thursday’s 2-0 Carabao Cup victory over Luton was our first shutout in any competition since the 1-0 win in last season’s FA Cup semi-final grudge-match with Leeds United, who will now be our next opponents in the League Cup. Apart from opening his goals account at the first attempt, Morgan Rogers set up five chances for team-mates at Fulham, the most by a Chelsea debutant since the statistic was first recorded in 2003/04. Joao Pedro’s 31-second opener at Fulham was the fastest ever over the first weekend of the Premier League season and quickest by a Chelsea player since the other Pedro’s strike against Man Utd in October 2016. 19 seconds - 8 October 1994 - John Spencer vs Leicester City (h)24 seconds - 12 September 1998 - Gianfranco Zola vs Nottingham Forest (h)28 seconds - 3 October 1999 - Gustavo Poyet vs Manchester United (h)29 seconds - 21 February 2004 - Eidur Gudjohnsen vs Arsenal (h)30 seconds - 23 October 2016 - Pedro vs Manchester United (h)31 seconds - 24 August 2026 - Joao Pedro vs Fulham (a)

news.title: Danny Welbeck: Brighton reunion will be special
news.body_en: After a long and storied career in the Premier League, Danny Welbeck is well-versed when it comes to facing former clubs, but Sunday’s meeting with Brighton & Hove Albion will still hold extra significance for the Chelsea striker. There is a familiar feel to Sunday’s fixture for Welbeck. A career spent representing several Premier League clubs means the experienced forward has often found himself lining up against former team-mates. That will be the case once more when Chelsea face Brighton this weekend. Yet familiarity will not diminish the significance of the occasion. Brighton remain an important part of Welbeck’s story, making Sunday a fixture he is eagerly anticipating. ‘It’s a special one because Brighton are my former team,’ Welbeck said. ‘Fortunately for me, I’ve played against my old teams quite a lot during my career, so it isn’t anything too new. ‘I’m really looking forward to it and I’m excited to keep pushing on.’ The game will provide another opportunity for Welbeck to build on a smooth start to life at Chelsea. Moving to a new club inevitably brings a period of adjustment, with different surroundings, team-mates and working methods to become accustomed to. However, the forward has felt at home from the moment he arrived at Cobham. He has been grateful for the warmth shown by his new team-mates, the staff and the Chelsea supporters, while the presence of several familiar faces helped make his transition even easier. Throw in a debut goal against Luton Town on Thursday night and it's fair to say Welbeck is enjoying life as a blue. ‘I’ve really enjoyed it and it has been pretty easy for me to settle,’ he explained. ‘It’s such a great group and the staff are very welcoming in and around the training ground. ‘Everybody has been great with me and I’ve been received really well by the fans, so I really appreciate that. ‘It was also nice to know a few familiar faces when I walked through the door, which helped me settle. Now I just want to keep building and improving every single day.’ Welbeck is also enjoying the early stages of working under new manager Xabi Alonso. The Blues are still adapting to Alonso’s methods, with new tactical information being introduced and players returning to the group at different stages following the World Cup and injuries. Welbeck believes patience and hard work will be required as those ideas take shape, but he has been encouraged by the opening weeks and is excited about what lies ahead. ‘It’s been really good and it has been a positive start, but we’re only a couple of games in,’ he added. ‘We have to keep working hard and keep learning the new ideas he is bringing to us. ‘There are a lot of new messages, while some players came back a little later and new players are being integrated and having to settle. But it has been really good up until now and there are really exciting times ahead.’

news.title: Alonso: Acheampong is getting better and better
news.body_en: Xabi Alonso highlighted the recent development of young defender Josh Acheampong, who has started the 2026/27 season in impressive form. The Chelsea Academy graduate was part of the senior squad last season, but has come into his own under Alonso’s guidance, playing every minute of competitive action for our Spanish manager so far. After helping us to make a winning start to the Premier League campaign against Fulham last weekend and book our place in the Carabao Cup third round with a clean-sheet win over Luton Town in midweek, Alonso explained why he has been impressed by the 20-year-old. ‘With Josh, in pre-season we saw that he has been getting better and better,’ said the Chelsea manager, ahead of Sunday’s meeting with Brighton & Hove Albion. ‘For me, when he plays with confidence and aggressiveness, he has a lot of attributes for a modern defender because he can play in different positions, he’s good with the ball, and he understands his role. ‘I’ve seen a progression in these few weeks we have been together and he has played very solid games against Fulham and Luton. We are happy that he is feeling this way and we need to help him. ‘There will be different moments in the season for sure, because we want to have healthy competition in all positions. But Josh is doing well and we’re happy for him, and he is happy as well.’

news.title: Cole Palmer on playing free alongside Morgan Rogers
news.body_en: Cole Palmer has revealed the conversations he had over the summer with Xabi Alonso and Morgan Rogers that helped him feel ready to produce his best on the pitch at Chelsea this season. Our No10 found it difficult to match the brilliant form of his previous two campaigns with the Blues last season, when his efforts were hindered by injury. However, joined in the line-up by old friend and new team-mate Rogers, under the guidance of manager Alonso, he has made a strong start to the 2026/27 Premier League. That was seen when he provided the assist for Joao Pedro to give us the lead just 31 seconds into our league opener, Rogers also getting on the score sheet before Palmer netted the winner himself, in a 3-2 victory over Fulham. ‘I just felt joy, really, and a bit of disbelief, because I didn't think we were going to score that quick,’ admitted Palmer. That win at Craven Cottage was the first glimpse of former Manchester City academy team-mates Palmer and Rogers in competitive action together for Chelsea, combining to provide the creative spark. ‘I think we're two different players,’ Cole added, when asked about that combination with Morgan. ‘He's more physical, more powerful and stuff, and I'm more technical and whatnot. ‘I just told him [when he joined] that he'll make a big difference. We're signing other players as well, so we're going to have a good team and we can do something good.’ As well as new team-mates, Palmer is playing under a new manager, following Alonso’s arrival in the dugout over the summer, and shared the main message he received from the Spaniard. ‘He just said to be free, because he knows what I can do when I feel good and I feel like I can go wherever on the pitch and find areas where I can cause damage. That's what he's told me.’ All of that leaves Palmer confident he can be back at his very best in 2026/27, although he revealed it is the mental impact of playing free of injury which he believes will make the biggest difference. ‘There were many things last season. Mainly just injury, though. It's just like, because you've been injured and then you're going out thinking, “oh, can I do certain things?”, kind of overthinking things. ‘It’s like, you're not doing things that you used to be able to do because previously it would hurt if you did it and whatnot. But I'm over that now.’ The evidence of that is clear on the pitch, after Palmer helped us open the new season with a league win over Fulham before booking our place in the Carabao Cup third round by beating Luton Town on Thursday evening. Next up, Palmer and Rogers will be hoping to combine to great effect again in our first home Premier League game of 2026/27, when we host Brighton & Hove Albion at Stamford Bridge on Sunday.

news.body_en: A special matchday programme for our first home Premier League fixture pays tribute to Ken Bates and Bobby Tambling. Meanwhile, goal-scoring legend Tambling is remembered in a touching tribute by his former room-mate and strike partner Barry Bridges, who recalls decades of friendship. Referring to his mate as 'an absolute gem', he reflects on their joint dream debut against West Ham United in February 1959. 'Making your debut for Chelsea is one thing, but to go through it all with such a good friend just made it even more special. And for both of us to score was like a dream. You just couldn’t script it. 'The next morning we went to the newsagents and bought a copy of every paper.' Elsewhere in the programme, we introduce new signing Marco Palestra with an exclusive interview, as the reigning Serie A Defender of the Year looks ahead to life at Chelsea. news.title: Under-18s report: Chelsea 6-1 Reading
news.body_en: An Andrew Pennie hat-trick helped Chelsea Under-18s make it three wins in a row with an emphatic 6-1 victory over Reading at Cobham. Chelsea produced some slick passing on a wet day in Surrey and wasted no time racing into an early lead through Isaac McGillvary and Heze Grimwade's goals. Pennie and Jacob Dako got in on the fun and, although Reading pulled a goal back, the game was all but over as a contest by the half-time break. Not letting our foot off the gas as the rain fell harder in the second half, Pennie found the net twice more to complete his hat-trick and ensure he would take the match ball home, while all three points would be staying in Cobham with the Blues. Reading had lost all four of their games so far this season and that lack of confidence showed in some early loose passes by the away side, and they soon realised why Cobham is such an unforgiving place to visit in that kind of form. Riley Ebho and Grimwade carried plenty of threat down the right straight from the off, but it was from the other flank our early opener arrived. By that time, in the eighth minute, Trey Faromo-Adebayo had already had one goal ruled out for offside. This time there was no flag to Reading’s rescue. Faromo-Adebayo’s strong run down the left created the opportunity when he found McGillvary towards that corner of the box, and our No10 made no mistake with a powerful strike to give Chelsea the lead. It had been coming and there was little surprise when we added a second soon afterwards. McGillvary was denied a second by the goalkeeper, but Grimwade reacted well to turn an awkwardly looping rebound into the empty net on the volley, for his third goal already this season. Chelsea kept pushing despite our two-goal lead, Jacob Hall doing well to step in to win possession high up the pitch and feed Faromo-Adebayo on the left, but he couldn’t find the target with a low drive. It was a sign of the Blues’ relentless attacking approach, which the Royals had little answer to. Although things quietened down for a bit, just after the half-hour mark we had another. Pennie got his first as he held a defender at arm’s length and smashed a shot into the top corner, but Grimwade gets plenty of credit too for his defence-splitting pass to find the striker in space. As the half-time break approached, Chelsea were increasingly dominant of possession, and a long team move of one and two-touch passes stretched our advantage further. The patient build-up accelerated in an instant when Grimwade flicked the ball into the path of Dako, who carried it across the edge of the box before skimming his shot across the wet pitch to nestle into the bottom corner. With the last kick of the first half, Reading pulled one back, as Jeremiah Berkeley-Agyepong scored from a tight angle just days after leaving Chelsea to join the Royals, but it already felt like too little too late for the visitors. This year's long, hot summer felt very much over as the rain really began to lash down at Cobham in the second half, but it didn’t stop Chelsea’s ruthless pursuit of more goals. The keeper had to produce two good saves to deny Pennie and Dako inside the first minute after the restart. Grimwade struck the base of the left-hand post with a curling free-kick and Calvin Diakite couldn’t get enough power on his header with a good opportunity, but with 15 minutes remaining Pennie showed his penalty box instincts twice to claim the match ball. A quick give-and-go between Pennie and Grimwade on the edge of the Reading box allowed the former to spin into the space behind the back line and calmly roll his finish past the keeper. When Reading stood off substitute Ibrahim Rabbaj, allowing him to lift a pinpoint cross to the back post, Pennie eluded his marker to complete his hat-trick and a 6-1 victory with a simple header. With back-to-back wins in the Under-18 Premier League, Chelsea move up to fourth place, three points behind leaders Tottenham Hotspur at this early stage of the season. Chelsea Under-18s will be back in league action next Saturday 5 September, when we travel to neighbours Fulham for an 11am kick-off, which CFC+ subscribers will be able to watch live on the Chelsea Official App and website. news.title: Xabi Alonso explains how 'great influence' Danny Welbeck raises standards
news.body_en: Danny Welbeck has a history of scoring in fixtures between Chelsea and Brighton & Hove Albion. Thankfully, when the two sides meet tomorrow at Stamford Bridge, he will be trying to do so for the Blues. Before moving to the Bridge this summer, Welbeck spent six years with the Seagulls and became a thorn in the Blues' side.  He netted six goals and claimed two assists for Brighton in nine Premier League meetings with Chelsea, the most recent of which came in April. Welbeck displayed his goal-scoring instincts in a Chelsea shirt for the first time on Thursday. The 35-year-old was handed his debut in our Carabao Cup second-round tie against Luton Town, and he opened the scoring with a well-taken header. Whether Welbeck features in tomorrow's contest in west London is a decision for Blues manager Xabi Alonso. The Spaniard knows the qualities the striker provides – and is pleased Welbeck will not be lining up for Brighton on this occasion. 'I am aware [of his record in the fixture] and I am happy he is with us!' joked Alonso in his pre-match press conference. 'He has many qualities. As a player, you see how intelligent he is, and he links well. Out of the box, he is able to combine, and in the box he is very intelligent to be in the right place. We saw that [against Luton]. 'On a daily basis, he is a great influence for the rest of the players. He trains really hard and is raising all the standards in training. This is something we think is important.' While Welbeck and fellow summer arrival Jordan Henderson have brought a wealth of experience to the Blues squad, Alonso has been keen to stress the influence of several other players within the first-team group. 'They [Henderson and Welbeck] help but it’s not just them,' said Alonso. 'Reece [James], Maxence [Lacroix], Morgan [Rogers] as well. Even if they are younger, they have a good impact. 'That was a very important decision in the squad planning - that we were bringing players who add not just on the field, but are ready to compete and who don’t need much time to make an impact. We are happy with that.'

news.body_en: Chelsea Women’s Under-18s made a superb start to their senior Women’s National League Cup campaign with a commanding 6-0 victory away at Wycombe Wanderers Women Chelsea N'Drin opened the scoring from the penalty spot on the half-hour and the Blues then struck five times after the interval, as Tess Finn, N'Drin again, Carla Gardiner, Maisie Brickell and Rebekah Pierce also found the net. Leanne Champ's side created a host of chances and dealt impressively with the physicality of their senior opponents, combining sharp transition play with composed finishing while keeping a clean sheet. Chelsea were made to work for the opening goal by a physical Wycombe side, but our youngsters continued to create chances and our positive play down the right was rewarded after 30 minutes. Gabi Storey, Keira Johnson and Brickell combined before the latter drove into the penalty area. Brickell skipped beyond three Wycombe players and was eventually brought down, leaving the referee to point to the spot. N'Drin stepped up and converted with power and placement into the corner, giving Chelsea a deserved lead that we carried into the interval. The Blues resumed with real purpose and doubled the advantage two minutes into the second half. Storey and Johnson combined on the right, with the latter delivering a low cross into the area. N'Drin's first effort was blocked, but Jahyma Putman recovered possession and spun before finding Finn on the edge of the box. The midfielder drove forward and finished across goal. Chelsea's reaction to a Wycombe throw-in brought the third goal on 57 minutes. Brickell won the first contact high up the pitch and Johnson controlled the ball before turning and releasing N'Drin on the right side of the area. The forward spotted the goalkeeper advancing from her line and produced a composed chip to claim her second goal. Gardiner was introduced in place of N'Drin after 65 minutes and needed only one minute to make an impact. Patient build-up play was recycled to goalkeeper Freya Weeks, whose long diagonal pass cleared the Wycombe defence and found Putman. Her early cross was met first time by the arriving Gardiner to make it 4-0. Chelsea added a fifth on 81 minutes after reacting quickly to regain possession in the middle third. Gardiner found Pierce on the left and the substitute drove inside before playing through Wycombe's defensive line for Brickell, who supplied a composed finish. There was still time for one final goal in the second minute of stoppage time. Chelsea won the first and second balls from a long Wycombe goal-kick, allowing captain Belle Sullivan to combine with Finn in midfield. Finn passed into Pierce's forward run and the substitute advanced into space before sending a superb long-range finish dipping beneath the crossbar. The emphatic victory puts Chelsea at the top of Group D after the opening round of Women's National League Cup fixtures, with two group matches remaining. Chelsea return to Professional Game Academy South League action on Sunday 30 August, when Crystal Palace visit. news.title: Jorja Fox leaves Chelsea
news.body_en: Chelsea can confirm defender Jorja Fox has today completed a permanent move to Ipswich Town. Fox joined the Chelsea Academy at the age of eight and made her senior debut for the Blues in a 4-0 away victory against Aston Villa in the 2020/21 campaign. Later that season, she made her first start in a 5-0 win over London City Lionesses. Her first professional contract with the club came in August 2021, on the day she turned 18. Loans to Charlton Athletic, Brighton and Hove Albion and Crystal Palace followed as she gained experience at senior level. Fox signed a contract extension with Chelsea in August 2024 and last season joined Newcastle United on a further loan. On the international stage, Fox represented England at every youth level during her time with the Blues. Everyone at Chelsea would like to wish Jorja every success in her future career.

news.title: Important information on Stamford Bridge bag policy
news.body_en: Ahead of Chelsea's first Premier League home match of the 2026/27 season, we would like to remind supporters of the bag policy in place at Stamford Bridge. The Terrorism (Protection of Premises) Act 2025, also known as ‘Martyn’s Law’, will come into effect in the UK in 2027. The legislation will require the club to demonstrate enhanced and robust security arrangements for everyone attending our home games. The bag policy is one of the measures we have in place for the safety and security of everyone attending our matches. To help maintain a safe environment and support quicker entry to Stamford Bridge, only bags no larger than A4 size are permitted. The maximum permitted dimensions are 30cm × 20cm × 10cm, approximately the size of a standard handbag. In anticipation of the requirements under Martyn’s Law, the bag policy will be strictly applied for all home matchdays at Stamford Bridge. Any bag that exceeds these dimensions will not be permitted into the stadium. The club strongly recommends that supporters avoid bringing bags to Stamford Bridge where possible. Supporters bringing a permitted bag should allow extra time for entry, as all bags are subject to search. While the club does not provide a bag storage facility at the stadium, options are available in the local area, including a matchday bag drop provided by Fulham Broadway Shopping Centre. You can find more information about this bag drop by clicking here. Any bag storage services in the local area are operated independently and are not affiliated with or controlled by the club. Exemptions to bag size restrictions will continue to be available for supporters who need to bring accessibility or medical equipment. More information on requesting a medical exemption can be found by clicking this link.

news.title: Alonso Press Conference 🎙️
Xabi Alonso confirms Chelsea team news for Brighton visit
news.body_en: Xabi Alonso is hopeful Chelsea midfielder Moises Caicedo will be ready to face Brighton & Hove Albion on Sunday, and says Levi Colwill and Geovany Quenda are in contention to face the Seagulls. Our third game of the week comes in the Premier League, as we welcome Fabian Hurzeler's side to Stamford Bridge. It is an opportunity for the Blues to make it three wins from three matches at the start of the campaign. Our latest victory came on Thursday evening as we defeated Luton Town in the Carabao Cup second round. Alonso selected a strong side, with a Danny Welbeck header and an own goal from Hakeem Odoffin sealing our progression to the third round. Neither Colwill nor Quenda were involved against the Hatters. Yet Alonso stressed there was no reason for concern, with both players being managed through a busy week. He explained: ‘There were no issues, and the plan is that they are training [from Friday] and preparing for the game on Sunday. 'With Levi, after his injury last season, he is still in a period where he has to take the right steps, we don’t want to push him too much. We want to make sure [his body] doesn't get stressed and that he feels comfortable and well. It’s the same with Geo as well.’ Caicedo hasn't yet featured for the Blues this season due to what, ahead of our opening fixture, Alonso detailed as a setback suffered in training. However, the Blues boss is hopeful the Ecuadorian will train ahead of the visit of his former club and be available for selection come Sunday's game. Alonso said: ‘He is hopefully training [on Friday] and we are hopeful that he can be involved [against Brighton]. But we need to check. No decision has been made.’ One player expected to be in contention to return for the Blues on Sunday is Wesley Fofana, who served the second of his two-match suspension against Luton. Summer signing Jordan Henderson, meanwhile, may need more time, with Alonso confirming in his pre-match press conference that the Blues are waiting for him to be given the 'green light to play soon' following the injury he sustained during the World Cup.

news.title: Analysis: How POTM Estevao provided Chelsea’s spark
news.body_en: We take a detailed look at Estevao Willian’s role in Chelsea’s Carabao Cup victory over Luton Town after he was voted as our Player of the Match by the Blues supporters. The Blues booked our place in the third round of this season’s Carabao Cup – where we will take on old rivals Leeds United – by defeating Luton 2-0 at Stamford Bridge on Thursday evening. Estevao played a key role in our victory. The Brazil international had a hand in both our goals and earned 34 per cent of votes in our Player of the Match ballot on the Chelsea Official App. Here's why... Having come off the bench in our Premier League opener away at Fulham, Estevao was handed his chance to impress new manager Xabi Alonso from the start in our first home game of 2026/27. That came as Alonso shifted to a 4-2-3-1 shape for his starting line-up – and it is a system that suits the Brazilian winger well. Operating on the right, Estevao was able to drift inside onto his left foot. Along with Morgan Rogers doing the same on the opposite flank, the two wide men were able to link up with Cole Palmer and striker Danny Welbeck ahead of him to overload Luton’s defence in the centre of the pitch. Estevao’s movement from that right-wing also created space for the marauding Malo Gusto to use his pace to overlap into promising crossing positions and create chances. It was that which led to Chelsea’s opening goal shortly after half-time, when Estevao and Gusto combined well to give the Frenchman the chance to deliver a dangerous cross from wide, headed in by Welbeck to give the striker his first goal for the club. Chelsea dominated the ball against our League One opponents; clear from our 65.7 per cent share of possession on the night. It allowed us to take the game to Luton and play high up the pitch, giving Estevao ample opportunity to operate where he does best, causing problems deep into opposition territory. As always, the Brazilian’s ability when running with the ball was a big part of that. His five dribbles were the most of any player on the pitch and he successfully completed four of them, also the highest number of the game. He had the end product to make those dribbles count too, with his six crosses the most of any player and five chances created, the joint-best alongside Palmer. Palmer was also the only player to register more than Estevao’s four shots across the 90 minutes, and it was one of those by the latter which made our victory safe, when the Brazilian’s low drive was deflected in off Luton defender Hakeem Odoffin, officially being recorded as an own goal.

news.title: Chelsea Football Club announces Circle Internet Group as Principal Partner
news.body_en: Chelsea Football Club today announces a landmark partnership with Circle Internet Group, Inc, one of the world’s leading internet financial platform companies. The new partnership sees Circle become a Principal Partner and our official front-of-shirt partner beginning with the 2026/27 season. The partnership comes at a pivotal moment for the world. Stablecoins are moving from early adoption toward the mainstream, creating an unprecedented opportunity to make money as open, accessible, and useful as the internet itself. By reducing the cost and friction of moving value, they can broaden participation in the global economy and unlock greater opportunity for people everywhere. Bringing USDC to one of sport’s biggest global stages reflects the scale and ambition of this opportunity. Founded in 2013, Circle is a pioneer in digital assets and is helping build the financial system for the internet. At its centre is USDC, the world’s leading regulated stablecoin. USDC is a trusted digital dollar that enables people and businesses to move money globally with internet speed and 24/7 availability. In the 2026/27 season, Circle and USDC brands will appear on the front of Chelsea's Men's, Women's and Academy shirts, featuring for the first time at Chelsea FC men’s first Premier League home game of the season this Sunday against Brighton. Jeremy Allaire, Co-Founder and CEO, Circle: 'We built USDC on the belief that money should work seamlessly for everyone everywhere, the way the internet does. Partnering with Chelsea connects us with a global sports community built on that exact same borderless vision. Kash Razzaghi, Chief Commercial Officer, Circle: 'This partnership represents a shared belief in where the world is headed. Chelsea connects hundreds of millions of people across every border, and USDC is digital money that moves across those same borders. USDC on the iconic Chelsea shirt shows the world what the future of global finance looks like: open, borderless, and built for everyone. Jason Gannon, President, Chelsea FC: 'This partnership with Circle positions Chelsea at the forefront of football’s digital evolution. We are two organisations fixated by the future and are relentlessly innovating to be in the best position possible for the long-term. We look forward to beginning our journey with Circle – to introduce Circle to the Chelsea family and continue enhancing how we operate' Aki Mandhar, CEO, Chelsea FC Women: ‘We are excited to introduce Circle and USDC to the Chelsea Women family for our inaugural season at Stamford Bridge. Forging and facilitating connections between people is what Chelsea Women and Circle do best and we look forward to bringing USDC to the CFCW fanbase and beyond.’ Todd Kline, President of Commercial, Chelsea FC: ‘Circle is changing how money moves around the world, and we’re changing what it means to be a global football club. That’s real alignment, not just in values but in our shared ambition to lead on a global stage. This is more than a logo on a shirt, it represents a partner who’s building something. We’re excited to see what we can build together.’ Don't miss out! Click here to register your interest and be the first to know when our newly branded 2026/27 home and away shirts go on sale!

news.title: Inside the life of Melvine Malard
news.body_en: After scoring a brace on her Chelsea debut against Real Sociedad, Melvine Malard fills us in on her footballing journey so far and how she likes to spend her time away from the sport. Can you tell us where you grew up and what it was like there? The name of the place is Ile de la Reunion. I played football over there. All my family is there. When I was 14 years old, I came to play football in a big club at Lyon. That's my life, and everything started from there. It’s very sunny there. Never cold. There are beaches, and there’s good food. You know, very, very colourful. What age did you start playing football? I started very late. About six or seven. At first, I didn’t really know that I would enjoy playing football. I played all sports, like boxing and handball with my sister. She was very good, and we played together. Afterwards, I tried football with the men because at that time it was only boys. I felt very confident in football, and then I said: 'That's going to be my job.' What was the name of your first grassroots team? The name was Saint-Denis FC. It’s the capital of La Reunion. Everything was with the boys over there. At first I didn’t play striker; I was a central defender. Then I moved forward to midfield and now striker, so it feels good to score in front of the people and in the big stadiums. Which person has influenced you the most in your career? I’m one of these people when you're born somewhere very far and are not rich. A godmother is someone who gives you the motivation to go forward in your life. So, I can say my godmother because in my family I don't have anyone who plays football, but she wanted me to follow my dreams. What's been the best moment of your career so far? I would like to say when you win something you work really hard for, like a trophy. Winning the Champions League was a really good memory for me. Of course, I have four Champions Leagues, but I only really played and started in two of them so I feel very proud of myself for those. I played some of those games in front of my family so you know, that’s the best part. Who are your best friends in football? My ball... (laughs). I actually don't have a very best friend, but it's true that in Manchester, I had some good friends over there, like Jade Riviere. She helped me a lot with everything, on and off the pitch. Manchester is a very good city, with very good people, and a very good atmosphere. Can you tell me your top three favourite footballers ever? I love Marta. Dzsenifer Marozsan. And Ronaldinho. He is a player, you know, where you watch, and you see he is not thinking; he is just playing and enjoying, and I love that. He did what his body wanted to do, not his head and played without fear. What do you like to do away from football? I really love to enjoy time with my family; that’s the most important thing. Now I have a wife, and I enjoy spending time with her. I love fashion. So I spend a lot of money on that passion! I also enjoy taking care of my body because my job is football, and I know that is very important. So, you know, recovery, staying home, enjoying the moment and relaxing. Are you watching any TV series at the moment? Who is your favourite music artist on Spotify? Ooh, I really love Shenseea. Burna Boy, too. Everything Afrobeat, you know? What are your top three places to go on holiday? I want to say Mexico. I love it there. I got engaged there. Of course, La Reunion. And I think Spain is the best also. If you had guests over for dinner, what would you cook for them? I really love sweet potatoes. I’d do them with bacon. Can you tell the Chelsea fans something they might not know about you? When you see me, you can see I love football, and I enjoy it when I play. I’m not thinking a lot when I'm on the pitch. So I want you to enjoy it with me! What's the best piece of advice you've ever received? Seriously, it's just like, don't forget where you were born. Where you come from. What does football mean to you? Football means everything. You know, I said to my sister this morning, if Melvine don't have football, it's not Melvine. Football gave me a reason to do well, mentally and physically.

news.title: Mamadou Sarr completes loan switch
news.body_en: Mamadou Sarr has completed a season-long loan move to Real Sociedad.
